outcome: Scoped implementation and new regressions complete; legacy fixture and shared type updates handed to integration.

contract.identity: AccountIdentity carries a private hashed lifecycle marker and a separate confirmed accountId hash. Only explicit confirmed identity can deduplicate. Email, nullable metadata, and legacy opaque lifecycle strings never prove identity.
contract.aggregate: Confirmed accounts use their freshest available lifetime counter once. Unresolved connections retain their own counters. total_tokens is a possibly duplicated connection sum when identity_complete=false; unresolved_connections explicitly counts enabled, non-removing connections without proof. accounts/reported_accounts then count aggregate groups, not proven distinct accounts.
contract.headline: Unresolved sums show an unverified badge, unresolved connection count, and may include duplicates. Missing counters remain partial; unresolved groups are not described as distinct-account coverage.
contract.history: History is retrieved before an independent allowance identity probe. Probe failure or absent/blank accountId clears prior proof before new history is accepted. This preserves successful history even if allowance times out and wedges its RPC process. Lifecycle changes invalidate both caches; plan-only changes do not.
contract.privacy: Raw identifiers remain provider-local. Neither lifecycle hashes nor confirmed identity hashes are exposed by account snapshots or persisted to analytics. Existing Accounts.read already captures the private identity with history under the cache lock.

Each history refresh adds a rateLimits identity probe and can wait for that probe timeout before publishing its successful history. A transient probe failure conservatively invalidates prior identity-bound caches, then publishes history without proof.
